messages:
mai: Quick idea — before we onboard the new 4-bit quant model, can we run a judge cohort diversity probe? want to catch regressions that only show up across judge mix.
ryan: +1. propose splitting judges into oracle / blind / cheap. oracle = main high-cap judge, blind = different priming, cheap = distilled smaller judge.
sophia: metrics to track: pairwise disagreement, Spearman rank corr, tie frequency, and subgroup breakdowns (prompt length, intent type). also epoch-level stability for repeat runs.
jordan: fyi: eval-runner had a nondet ordering bug last night; saw different tie counts between replays. suspect shuffle seed not hooked.
mai: can you paste the log snippet?
jordan: sure: ```
[2026-03-18T02:12:03Z] running judge panel: oracle-v2, cheap-distil, blind-primed
[2026-03-18T02:12:03Z] shuffle_seed=0x0a7f
[2026-03-18T02:12:03Z] WARNING: judge_order non-deterministic for same seed on rerun
```
ryan: I can patch runner to enforce stable ordering by default (sort by (example_id, judge_name) unless --shuffle). quick fix in PR 3456.
sophia: also recommend an adjudication fallback policy in the rubric: if no consensus, (1) prefer oracle, (2) if still tied, compare raw score deltas, (3) otherwise flip to meta-judge. draft below.
sophia: ```
Rubric v0.1 (for judge gating):
- consensus: >= 2/3 judges agree on winner => pass
- near-tie: max_score - runner_up_score < 0.05 => mark as tie
- tie-breaker order: oracle preference -> raw-score L1 delta -> rerun with new seeds -> meta-judge decision
- record: pairwise disagreement, tie_reason, subgroup tags
```
mai: add subgroup fairness checks too (length bins, gendered names, toxicity flag). we don't want regressions that only surface on 10% slices.
jordan: added a tiny smoke script: `scripts/ci/judge_cohort_smoke.sh` — runs 3 judges over 200 canned examples, outputs tie histogram.
mai: can you post the command?
jordan: ```bash
./scripts/ci/judge_cohort_smoke.sh --judges oracle-v2 cheap-distil blind-primed --size 200
```
eval-bot: automated run finished: judges=[oracle-v2,cheap-distil,blind-primed]; examples=200; ties=24; pairwise_disagreement_mean=0.18; spearman_rho=0.84
sophia: 24 ties /200 is high. whats current tie threshold? we use 0.05 by default.
ryan: maybe calibrate threshold per-task. for low-distinguish prompts tighten to 0.03. also consider using logits L1 as tie-breaker before reruns.
mai: action items: (1) ryan -> runner patch & unit test for stable ordering; (2) jordan -> add smoke script to CI matrix; (3) sophia -> formalize metrics and per-task thresholds and write rubric doc. target: land before quant rollout next week.
jordan: i'll open a PR to add smoke to `ci/smoke` with flag `--judge-cohort` :thumbsup:
ryan: opening runner PR now, will include deterministic-order unit test.
sophia: i'll author rubric.md and add Jupyter notebook to compute pairwise disagreement slices by subgroup. will link here when ready.
mai: any objections to 3-judge panel as initial gate? cheaper to iterate.
sophia: fine with 3 judges for gating, but recommend expanding to 5 for final acceptance runs.
ryan: fine.
eval-bot: scheduled: next automated cohort run 2026-03-23T10:00:00Z.
mai: perfect. thanks all — ping me on PRs and i'll prioritize reviews.
